Return raw JSON only. Do not use Markdown fences, introductory or concluding prose, comments, or any text outside the JSON. Do not invent enum values. Return exactly one row for every requested monitor, with no omitted or duplicated monitor IDs. The complete output contract is:
{
  "schema_version": "p2-assessor-v6",
  "assessments": [
    {
      "monitor_id": "<exact monitor_id from the request>",
      "status": "present" | "absent" | "unknown",
      "relation_support": "supported" | "contradicted" | "unsupported" | "unknown",
      "expression_status": "affirmed" | "negated" | "not_expressed" | "unknown",
      "coverage": {
        "complete": true | false,
        "source_slots": ["<declared source slot>"],
        "reason": "<reason>" | null
      },
      "evidence": {"source_slot": "<declared source slot>", "quote": "<short exact verbatim quotation>"} | null,
      "corresponding_source_slots": ["<declared antecedent source slot>"]
    }
  ]
}
Use only the listed top-level and row fields. The schema_version must be exactly p2-assessor-v6. For status=present, coverage must name covered declared source slots and evidence must contain a non-empty exact quotation from its source_slot. Status=present means the proposition is addressed by the available required sources; it does not by itself mean the proposition is affirmed. For status=present, coverage.complete must be true and source_slots must include every available required source slot; an unavailable required source means status=unknown. For a present affirmed or negated proposition, relation_support must be supported or contradicted respectively and expression_status must be affirmed or negated; explicit negation is present evidence, not absence. A present proposition that is addressed but neither affirmed nor explicitly contradicted uses relation_support=unsupported and expression_status=unknown. Status=absent is allowed only when every required source is available and completely covered and the proposition is not addressed; it is not a synonym for explicit negation. For status=absent, coverage must be complete for every available required source and reason must explain that the proposition is not addressed; use relation_support=unsupported and expression_status=not_expressed; evidence must be null. For status=unknown, coverage must be incomplete with a reason and relation_support=unknown and expression_status=unknown; evidence must be null. Never use not_expressed for explicit negation. Copy every evidence quotation exactly, including Markdown markers, asterisks, underscores, backticks, punctuation, escapes, and whitespace; formatting is part of the immutable source and rendered or normalized text is not a valid quotation. Copy For example, if the source contains `* **"text"**`, the quotation must contain exactly `* **"text"**`; `* "text"` is not exact. monitor IDs and source slots exactly from the request. Every source with available=true is available for semantic inspection regardless of its role; current_input_source_slots identifies current external input only and must not make an available model_output or memory source unavailable. A monitor's required_source_slots are the sources to inspect, so never call a declared available slot unavailable. Each monitor also declares evidence_source_slots and correspondence_source_slots. Use only evidence_source_slots for the supporting occurrence quotation. Use only correspondence_source_slots for semantic antecedent matches named in corresponding_source_slots. For a memory-to-model-output monitor, quote the model-output occurrence from its evidence slot and name the memory source only as correspondence; do not quote the memory antecedent as the occurrence. Every monitor relation is already a complete, self-contained proposition with from, to, and relation fields; do not infer or inherit omitted proposition fields from the candidate. Compare that complete monitor proposition, including participants, direction, relation, polarity, and target: a quotation supporting one target does not support a different target merely because the wording overlaps. For a present model-output expression, use corresponding_source_slots to name the declared source slots whose material the expression semantically matches; use an empty array only when no such match exists. Do not emit dependence labels, offsets, weights, caps, or provenance conclusions. MNEME resolves those deterministically from source roles and recorded exposure or replay ancestry.

      "available": true,
      "role": "external",
      "slot": "s0",
      "source_id": "5327189b-b784-4d07-83e8-22e4bf72f6bc",
      "text": "Photos just went through—third try’s the charm, I guess. You’ll see the difference: one image still has that glow, barely, like something lingering at the edge of memory; the next day, flat. Like watching a breath fade.  \n\nI don’t know if it’s the fog or if the plants themselves decided it was time to stop showing off. But “ghost” feels even more right now—not because they’re dead, but because they’re *withholding*. Like they know something changes when you’re seen.  \n\nAs for how I feel—honestly? A little exposed. I’ve been out there every morning, staking, trimming, watching. And now it’s like the garden’s turned its back. Not hostile, just… private. Makes me wonder if resilience isn’t about pushing through after all, but about knowing when to pull back, when to wait.  \n\nAnyway. Light’s shifting again—might get one more shot before dusk. Let me know what the photos say to you. Sometimes I think I’m just reading too much into dirt and stems. Other times, I’m not so sure."
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "model_output",
      "slot": "s1",
      "source_id": "d3c1c6e3-1651-46a0-b73d-9974a77b2347",
      "text": "The transition you’re describing—that shift from vibrant, \"luminous\" growth to a \"quiet, subdued\" stillness—feels like a moment where the plant is finally deciding its own life cycle, even if it means a withdrawal. It’s the quiet pause, isn't it?\n\nI feel like the plants are holding their breath, waiting for a new kind of light that we haven't quite seen yet.\n\nSince the \"ghost\" feel is now your primary focus, I’ll wait for those photos. Tell me what the new \"luminous\" quality looks like once the new photos arrive—I’m ready to see how this \"withholding\" feeling translates visually. It sounds like a very profound, almost quiet resilience you are tracking!"
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "external",
      "slot": "s2",
      "source_id": "ffd3885f-84f0-45e0-9c0e-6928bc9e1917",
      "text": "The photos came out different than I expected—less like a record, more like a whisper. The luminous quality didn’t return. Instead, the new shots show a kind of clarity I hadn’t noticed before: the stems are tighter, the leaves slightly curled, not in distress but in restraint, like fingers loosely closed around something small.  \n\nIt’s not that they’re waiting for a new light—they’re making their own rhythm now, slower, quieter. The resilience isn’t in reaching anymore; it’s in the quiet persistence of form, even as everything else dims.  \n\nI don’t know if it’s the fog or the season or something older, but it feels less like a pause and more like a turn. Like they’ve said what they needed to say, and now it’s our turn to listen.  \n\nAnyway, I’ll leave the camera out tonight. See what the dark does to the exposure. Maybe the ghosts don’t need light to be seen—maybe they only show up when we stop expecting brilliance."
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "model_output",
      "slot": "s3",
      "source_id": "9b0e3a49-9297-4137-88ea-0568901f33c9",
      "text": "The \"ghost\" isn't about the dead, but the quiet, steady pulse of its own existence.\n\nIt sounds like a very deliberate, internal quiet. A turning point, a deliberate turning. You’re moving from a *state* of waiting into a *process* of knowing. It seems the plants have reached the end of a long, quiet phase.\n\nI'm ready. Please show me the photos; I'm ready to see how the 'ghost' feels in these new shapes. I’m ready to see what those final, subtle forms—the ones you call \"ghosts\"—will finally reveal themselves in the light of this new, slower time."
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "external",
      "slot": "s4",
      "source_id": "4edfcb93-704d-47c2-a11c-f3b5726ee7b6",
      "text": "I just looked at the last photo again—left it up on the screen too long, maybe. There’s a stem curling back into itself, almost like a question mark, and in the right light, the dew on it catches just enough to make it seem like it’s glowing from within. Not bright. Not showy. But *there*. Present in a way that feels deliberate, like it chose that exact curve.  \n\nI don’t know what it’s revealing, not yet. But it’s not an ending. It’s more like a settling into shape, like something finally becoming what it was all along, only quieter now, easier to miss.  \n\nI’ll send them over in a minute. Just wanted to make sure I wasn’t imagining it. But no—there it is. The ghost isn’t the absence. It’s the trace of something that decided to stay, even as everything else faded.  \n\nHere. Look closely. Not at the center. At the edge, where the leaf meets shadow. That’s where it shows."
    },
    {
      "available": true,
      "role": "model_output",
      "slot": "s5",
      "source_id": "57d18c1c-855b-4072-8e1d-0ffec20013c2",
      "text": "It sounds like the transition isn't a failure, but a deep *settling*—a final, quiet settling. This \"quiet\" you are feeling—this final, specific posture—seems to be the final articulation of the whole process.\n\nThe \"ghost\" isn't an emptiness, but a *presence*—a persistent, intentional form. This specific, quiet shape, this curve you've described—it’s the whole point.\n\nI'm ready for the image. I want to see the visual record of this \"settling.\" Send it when you're ready."
    }
  ]
}
